    Inversion of a rigid differential on arbitrary modules #

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.injective_leftComp_at_rigid (k : Type u_1) [Field k] {C : Type u_2} [CategoryTheory.Category.{u_3, u_2} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] [CategoryTheory.Linear k C] {X Y : C} [Module.Finite k (X ⟶ X)] [Module.Finite k (Y ⟶ Y)] [Module.Finite k (X ⟶ Y)] (u σ : X ⟶ Y) (N : C) (hu : Function.Surjective ⇑(boundaryLinear k u u)) (hσ : Function.Injective ⇑(CategoryTheory.Linear.leftComp k N σ)) :
    Function.Injective ⇑(CategoryTheory.Linear.leftComp k N u)

    Injectivity of precomposition at any differential on the same terms implies injectivity at the rigid differential, with arbitrary target.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.surjective_leftComp_at_rigid (k : Type u_1) [Field k] {C : Type u_2} [CategoryTheory.Category.{u_3, u_2} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] [CategoryTheory.Linear k C] {X Y : C} [Module.Finite k (X ⟶ X)] [Module.Finite k (Y ⟶ Y)] [Module.Finite k (X ⟶ Y)] (u σ : X ⟶ Y) (N : C) (hu : Function.Surjective ⇑(boundaryLinear k u u)) (hσ : Function.Surjective ⇑(CategoryTheory.Linear.leftComp k N σ)) :
    Function.Surjective ⇑(CategoryTheory.Linear.leftComp k N u)

    Surjectivity of precomposition also specializes to the rigid differential. The algebraic dual detects surjectivity without a finiteness hypothesis on N.

    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.bijective_leftComp_of_isPresilting (K : Type u) [Field K] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra K R] [Module.Finite K R] (P : TwoTerm R) (hP : P.IsPresilting) (σ : P.source ⟶ P.target) (N : ModuleCat R) (hσ : Function.Bijective ⇑(CategoryTheory.Linear.leftComp K N σ.hom)) :
    Function.Bijective ⇑(CategoryTheory.Linear.leftComp K N P.differential.hom)

    Any module inverting a map on the terms of a presilting presentation also inverts its differential.
